title: Change evaluation: CR-014 team chat notification channel

sheets.name: Evaluation
rows: Is the change likely to substantively affect the security posture? (FRD-SGC)

Yes. It adds a third-party service in the alert delivery path (T6), a new outbound flow from the notification workers (P2), and a new kind of address stored with the routing policy (D2). Each of these changes the scope record.
I-16 What changes; I-14 P2; D2; PF3; third_party_resources; FRD-SGC; SCN-CSO-EVA
Is it likely to change the certification class? (FRD-CCC)
No. The request adds no new data class and describes no change to impact levels.
Does it recur routinely as part of ongoing operations? (FRD-RTR)
No. It is the first chat channel, and the change log has no earlier change of this kind.
I-16 What changes; I-13 entries; FRD-RTR
Does it introduce substantive risks that must be assessed in depth? (FRD-TRF)

Proposed yes, for the SME to confirm. The change adds a capability agencies configure and use, and a new third party that needs the MAS-CSO-TPR documentation. Against that, messages follow the existing payload policy (PF3), which could make it adaptive if the SME judges that existing checks verify it with minor changes. See DQ-001.
I-16 What changes; I-14 PF3; FRD-TRF; FRD-ADP; MAS-CSO-TPR
